basis: Written from the published specification and established practice in the field; no new sources were read. Unreviewed.

distinguishingFeatures: An enduring body that persists across meetings and changes of members.
Separates seats from their holders and the body from its parent organization.
Differs from a meeting, which is one session of the body.
Holds references to decisions without being a validity engine for them.

may: Resolve a body and its current mandate.
Record membership and term assertions from authoritative sources.
Check whether recorded attendance meets the body's stated quorum rule.
Prepare reports on mandate reviews and expiring terms.
mustNot: Infer binding authority from a committee name or chair title.
Cast votes, appoint members or convene meetings.
Apply a default quorum rule when the governing rule is unknown.
Remove dissent or contested states from the record.

considerations: Membership records reveal personal affiliations and must be handled carefully.
Accountability requires that decisions can be traced to the body and rules that made them.
Diversity and conflict-of-interest information is sensitive but matters for legitimacy.
affectedParties: People governed by the body's decisions

items: A governance body has a constituting instrument, a mandate, seats and procedural rules.
Confused with the organization, a meeting, a working group without mandate and a person's office.
Decisions treated as valid without quorum or authority.
Stale membership leading to wrong signatures.
W3C Organization Ontology posts and memberships.
Popolo specification for organizations, memberships and motions.
OASIS LegalDocML (Akoma Ntoso) for decisions and minutes.
